scope: Deployable web and worker container images, verified from an empty database and under Railway-like conditions. Railway provisioned on 2026-11-04: Postgres and the worker exist, the web service is not deployed.
verified: Both images build from their own Dockerfile's last stage, with no warning and no error, which is how Railway builds
23 migrations applied from the worker image onto an empty database, 0001 through 0023_sponsored_purchases.sql
/api/ready returns 503 DATABASE_NOT_READY with no database configured, exposing no detail
/api/health returns 200 with no DATABASE_URL configured at all, so liveness does not touch the database
/api/health reports the mode read from configuration, not a label written into the source

Started with --user 0:0 against a root-owned volume, the entrypoint drops privileges: /proc/1/status reports Uid 1000 1000 1000 1000, the volume becomes 1000:1000 mode 700, and /api/health reports privileged false
A configured evidence directory that cannot be written refuses to start with a structured reason and exit code 1
An unconfigured evidence directory starts and says out loud that artifacts are lost on redeploy
/ returns 307 to /sign-up with public signup enabled; /sign-up returns 200
The web image carries .next, node_modules, public, package.json and server.js, and no project source

resolved.finding: The bundler was tracing the whole project into the standalone server output because src/server/storage.ts resolves the private evidence directory at run time, which would copy every source file and all of public/ into the deployed server directory.
resolved.history: Recorded as three storage tracing warnings in every checkpoint since PRACTICE-01 and treated as cosmetic.
resolved.fix: The three dynamic filesystem calls are explicitly opted out of tracing; that directory is a mounted volume holding private evidence, never content to bundle.
resolved.foundBy: Building the image. npm run build in the repository shows the warnings but not the consequence.

notDone: Nothing is provisioned on Railway and no domain is held
No verified sending domain, so signup mail is unusable
No secret store, backup, verified restore, monitoring, retention or abuse control
Hosted execution is unavailable: Railway containers are non-privileged, and the runner host adapter shells out to the macOS-only orb CLI
An S3-compatible private evidence store becomes required once execution is hosted, because a Railway volume attaches to one service only
A deployment without hosted execution must report testing unavailable rather than queue tests that cannot run

host.cannotHost: the gVisor test runner, because Railway containers are non-privileged
host.provisionedBy: the user, from the runbook in docs/FREE-03.md

state.postgres: online, private, DATABASE_URL resolved to a private postgresql host on 5432
state.worker: deployed from Dockerfile.worker, crash-looping until migrations run

toVerifyOnFirstDeploy: Whether a custom Start Command preserves the image ENTRYPOINT; if it does not, the privilege drop is bypassed and /api/health reports privileged true. Still unanswered: the web service is not deployed

Whether the non-privileged-container and one-volume-per-service limits still hold, since they rest partly on staff replies and community threads. The no-build-target limit is now confirmed by the worker deploy

firstDeploy.confirmed: RAILWAY_DOCKERFILE_PATH builds the named file's last stage, so the one-file-per-service answer to Railway having no build target works in practice
firstDeploy.failure: The worker restarted eight times reporting worker.failed with no detail, because its catch logged the event name and discarded the error
firstDeploy.cause: The schema was never migrated. A Railway pre-deploy command runs only on the deploys that follow it, and the runbook set it after the first upload
firstDeploy.notTheCause: The DATABASE_URL reference resolved correctly, checked by printing only its shape - scheme, hostname presence, port, path - and never its value
firstDeploy.fix: workers/main.ts reports the SQLSTATE and the error message, with the message passed through the evidence redaction policy and the connection string supplied as a known secret
firstDeploy.reproduced: {"event":"worker.failed","code":"42P01","detail":"relation \"assignments\" does not exist"} against a fresh disposable local database, created and dropped for the purpose
firstDeploy.fixVerified: Applying the 23 migrations to that same database and re-running the worker produced no failure
firstDeploy.runbookCorrected: docs/FREE-03.md now sets the pre-deploy command before the first upload and records why

secondAttempt.result: Crashed the same way, and the new log line named the cause in one read: worker.failed code 42P01, relation "assignments" does not exist
secondAttempt.cause: The pre-deploy command had been typed into the dashboard and Railway had not saved it. serviceInstance.preDeployCommand reads null on the worker and on web, so it was not set on the wrong service: Railway stages dashboard configuration and applies it on a separate action
secondAttempt.notReported: Nothing in a deploy says a pre-deploy command is missing. There is no log line for a release step that does not exist
secondAttempt.authority: Railway public GraphQL API through railway api, not the dashboard appearance
secondAttempt.runbookCorrected: The dashboard step is replaced by serviceInstanceUpdate plus a serviceInstance read-back before the upload. preDeployCommand is [String!] in the live schema, an argv rather than a shell line, so the runbook passes ["sh","-c","node scripts/migrate.ts"]
secondAttempt.stillUnverified: Whether Railway accepts that mutation and runs the command. The field types come from live introspection and the read-back query is verified against the real service; the write and the deploy after it are the user’s
